title: Arm Triangle Threat
description: The attacker has moved the opponent’s arm across the neck line and is looking for shoulder pressure and angle to finish.
topPlayerGoals: The top player wants to control Arm Triangle Threat through Head Position, Inside Position, and directed pressure.
Isolate the arm, block elbow recovery, and finish with control.
Keep a stable base so you are not off-balanced or countered.
bottomPlayerGoals: The bottom player wants to survive Arm Triangle Threat with frames, Pummeling, or the right angle.
Pull the elbow back to the ribs, create a hip frame, and recover posture.
Recognize danger signals early instead of waiting for the position to settle.
controlPoints: Main control point: Arm across the neck, head block, and shoulder pressure.
Head, hands, hips, and knees should share the same force direction.
The Elbow-Knee Connection or hip-shoulder line determines whether the position is still alive or already locked.
escapePriorities: Escape priority: Bring the elbow back to the ribs before making a big bridge.
Protect the neck, back, Knee Line, or arm line before countering.
If Inside Position is lost, reset one defensive layer first.

advancementOptions.action: Walk the angle to the Side Control finish line
advancementOptions.why: This is the natural branch when you win the main control point and the opponent is forced to defend.

dangerSignals: The chin or neck is pulled out of a safe line.
The elbow separates from the ribs or knee.
The hip line is locked while the shoulder line is still being pulled.
You need a long hand post to avoid falling.
